speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the neck swelling for me, specifically how long it has been there and whether it is painful or growing rapidly?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of colon cancer, I need to ask if you have experienced any recent unintentional weight loss, night sweats, or changes in your bowel habits? REQUEST TEST: Neck_ Ultrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Ultrasound_of_the_Neck: Well-circumscribed lesion in the subcutaneous tissue suggestive of a cystic nature.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of trauma to the area, or have you noticed any changes in the size of the swelling with neck movement? REQUEST TEST: Fine_Needle_Aspiration

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal FNA results suggest the lesion is not a simple cyst or typical lymph node, which is concerning given your history of colon cancer. I need to rule out metastatic disease or a soft tissue tumor, so I will order a biopsy for definitive histology. REQUEST TEST: Biopsy_of_Neck_Mass

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Biopsy_of_Neck_Mass: Histology shows mature adipose tissue with a thick fibrous capsule, consistent with an intracapsular lipoma.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy confirms this is a benign intracapsular lipoma, which explains the slow growth and lack of pain. Since the lesion is well-circumscribed and non-malignant, we can rule out metastatic colon cancer at this site. DIAGNOSIS READY: Intracapsular Lipoma
